nv_pine_tree_ledge.blurb: Pine Tree Ledge is a bolted limestone shelf in the Hood zone of Mount Charleston, in the mountains above Las Vegas. All twelve climbs are sport routes, and the grades lean hard: one in the 5.10s, a couple at 5.11, a big block of 5.12 and two 5.13s. It is known for a good run of 5.12 lines and a few warm-ups to start the day. Only a handful of distinct starts are shared among the routes, so a busy day gets crowded. You reach the ledge by a short, slick scramble up from the cave below, which is not a great fit for small kids or dogs.

nv_upper_rift.blurb: Upper Rift is a small sandstone sport crag in Calico Basin, Red Rock, tucked above the corridor of The Rift. Its twelve routes are short and mostly punchy, with an easy start leading to a steep one- or two-move crux. Grades cluster around 5.10, with a single 5.8, one 5.11 and one 5.12. Easier lines sit toward the left side, moderates in the middle and the harder ones to the right. The wall sits in shade early and picks up sun once the morning wears on, around 10 or 11. Reach it by scrambling past the boulder jam at the corridor's end or by going around the right side under Bowling Ball wall.

nv_pit_ledges_right.blurb: Pit Ledges (right) is a stretch of steep sport climbing on the south side of Hercules Gap, a limestone slot canyon near Ely in eastern Nevada. It carries on from the Cave Sector routes and is reached by walking west along the base of the southern cliff. Twelve bolted lines run from the 5.10s up to the low 5.13s, and this is a place for strong climbers: six of them sit at 5.12 and three at 5.13, with only a few easier ones. Most routes earn a moderate rating from visitors, and a couple of the hardest ones are standouts.

nv_pirate_s_cove.blurb: Pirate's Cove is a small sport crag along the Kyle Canyon road on Mount Charleston, west of Las Vegas. A dozen bolted routes are split between a left wall and a right wall roughly a hundred yards apart. Grades sit mostly around 5.11, with a pair of 5.10s and a handful of 5.12s. The rock is rougher than elsewhere on the mountain, but the routes are fun, and the cliff stays in shade for most of the day, which makes it a cool choice when the valley is hot. The approach is a short hike of about ten minutes from the trailhead.

nv_chicken_leg.blurb: Chicken Leg is a trad wall in the lower part of Keyhole Canyon, in the Eldorado Mountains of southern Nevada, set on the outside of a bend in the wash. It holds a dozen routes, almost all traditional single pitches on granite, from about 5.8 to 5.10 with one short aid line. Routes run up to about 100 feet and there are no bolted anchors, so bring a rack and slings; some lines can be top-roped by building your own anchor. The wall takes its name from a drumstick-shaped feature beside the main crack. A couple of climbs are runout or have dubious gear low down, so this is not a beginner wall.

nv_armory_wall.blurb: Armory Wall is a section of Castle Rock above Stateline on the Nevada side of Lake Tahoe, where the featured, steep-for-its-grade rock gives deep jugs. Most of the dozen routes are bolted, with a couple of trad lines, and the grades are friendly: the bulk run from about 5.6 to 5.8, with a very easy one at the bottom and a single 5.11 at the top end. Climbs mostly face west, so the lake views are wide, and there is shade early in the day near the trees and in the gully. A bit of scrambling is needed to reach the left side of the wall.
